title: Vague request (gate demo)
summary: Shows how the analyst handles missing information

input.request: We need a better system for our team. The current way of doing things is not working well and people are frustrated.
We need a better system for our team. The current way of doing things is not working well and people are frustrated.

questions.question: What specific business problem or process is failing, and what does 'not working well' mean in concrete terms (e.g., too slow, too many errors, lacking a feature)?
questions.rationale: Without a defined problem statement, requirements cannot be derived; 'a better system' is not actionable.

questions.question: Who are the members of 'our team' and what is the team's function or department?
questions.rationale: The user base and their roles must be known to define functional requirements and access needs.

questions.question: What is the current system or process being used today (name, tool, or manual method)?
questions.rationale: Without knowing the existing system, it's impossible to assess what data, integrations, or migration needs exist.

questions.question: Who else, beyond the immediate team, is affected by or interacts with this process (e.g., managers, other departments, external parties)?
questions.rationale: Unidentified stakeholders could be impacted by changes or need to approve the solution, risking incomplete requirements.

questions.question: What specifically is causing frustration for people using the current system or process?
questions.rationale: Frustration could stem from many different root causes (usability, speed, errors, missing features); the fix depends entirely on the cause.

questions.question: Is this request for a new system, a replacement of an existing tool, or an enhancement/process change to the current way of working?
questions.rationale: This determines whether the project is a build, buy, migrate, or process redesign effort, which drastically changes scope and approach.

questions.question: Who has the authority to approve requirements and sign off on the final solution?
questions.rationale: Without a defined approver, requirements cannot be validated or finalized.

questions.question: What data does the team currently work with, where is it stored, and does it include any personal or sensitive information?
questions.rationale: Data location and sensitivity affect architecture, security, and compliance requirements; without this, those areas cannot be scoped.

questions.question: Are there any existing systems or tools that the new solution would need to integrate with?
questions.rationale: Unidentified integration needs could be discovered late, causing rework.

questions.question: What industry or regulatory context does the team operate in, and are there compliance or data retention obligations to consider?
questions.rationale: Industry was not provided; without it, applicable regulations cannot be identified, risking a non-compliant solution.

questions.question: How will the business measure whether the new system has successfully solved the problem?
questions.rationale: Without success criteria, it will be impossible to validate the project's outcome or know when it is complete.

questions.question: Are there any known constraints on budget, timeline, technology platform, or staffing that will limit the solution?
questions.rationale: Constraints shape feasible options; none were provided, so assumptions may lead to an unworkable design.

questions.question: Who should have access to the system, and are there different permission levels needed for different roles?
questions.rationale: Access control design depends on knowing user roles and sensitivity of functions/data.

questions.question: What is the expected volume of use (number of users, transactions, or records) the system needs to support?
Is there a preferred timeline or urgency driving this request, such as a specific deadline or event?

problem.problem_statement: A team is experiencing frustration with its current way of working, but the specific process, system, or pain points causing this frustration are not identified in the request.

objectives.description: Reduce team frustration by improving the current way of doing things.
Replace or improve an unspecified process or system to make the team's work more effective.

target_users: Members of the team referenced in the request (specific roles unknown)
problem.current_state: An unspecified 'current way of doing things' exists that is causing frustration among team members.
problem.future_state: An improved system or process that reduces frustration, though the desired characteristics of this future state are not specified.
ambiguities: 'Better system' is undefined — unclear whether this refers to a software system, a business process, a team structure, or something else.
'The current way of doing things' is not described, so the specific pain points are unknown.
'People are frustrated' does not specify who is frustrated, why, or how frustration manifests (e.g., delays, errors, communication issues).
No indication of which team (department, function, size) is affected.
No indication of whether a technical solution, process change, or organizational change is expected.
missing_information: What industry or business domain the team operates in
Who the stakeholders and end users are (roles, departments)
What the current process or system consists of, and what specific tasks it supports
What specific problems or symptoms are causing frustration (e.g., delays, errors, manual work, lack of visibility)
Whether 'system' refers to software, a business process, an organizational structure, or a combination
Any existing tools, systems, or platforms currently in use
Any constraints such as budget, timeline, compliance requirements, or technical limitations
What success would look like if the problem were solved
